clue.text: Old homosexual?'s reaction to last orders?

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for a young man kept by an older male lover, now obsolete
read as two words, the rush to the counter of a pub when the landlord calls last orders

explanation.surface: A quip about how an elderly gay man responds when the pub calls time.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British pub the landlord calls 'last orders' shortly before closing, prompting a dash to the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare archaic noun once named a catamite, so the setter flags it as an old term with a question mark.

clue.text: One sort of muscle raised in encore for another

indicators.note: in means the muscle goes inside the cry of encore

parts.note: bis is a call for an encore

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards

parts.note: pec is short for pectoral muscle

explanation.surface: One muscle shown off during an encore in place of another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns PEC to CEP, put 'in' BIS. The definition 'another' means another muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: The biceps is a different muscle from the pectoral, so it is 'another' sort.

clue.text: Haphazard money order

parts.note: the rand is South African money
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A random money transfer.
explanation.definitionFit: Random and haphazard both mean done without plan or pattern.

clue.text: A secret service once pursuing an American Church Father

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the first chunk follows the article an

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Stasi was East Germany's secret police, now defunct
US means American

explanation.surface: A Cold War spy agency chases an American theologian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursuing' means the A plus the secret service come after the article; 'Church Father' is a pope, not a priest who is a dad.
explanation.definitionFit: Anastasius was the name of several early popes and Church leaders, among the Fathers of the Church.

clue.text: Animal put on dark work clothes, etc

definitions.text: put on dark work clothes, etc
definitions.meaning: a word that follows dark, work, clothes and others to make familiar compounds

explanation.definitionFit: The animal's name completes dark ___, work___, clothes ___ and many more phrases.

clue.text: Unhealthy eater's backing group crosses one major road

indicators.note: crosses means straddles, so the reversed group holds the next pieces inside
backing means the group's word is read from right to left

parts.note: a club is a group of members
one is the Roman numeral I
the M1 is Britain's major motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A group of backing singers with an eating disorder drives across a big highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns CLUB to BULC, which 'crosses' I and MI (the M1 motorway, London to Leeds) by holding them. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with bulimia binges and purges, so a sufferer is described by this adjective used as a noun.

clue.text: The city for curry (with second helpings)

parts.note: a balti is a kind of curry
more is what you ask for as a second helping

explanation.surface: The town known for its curry, if you come back for more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' links; a balti is a curry popular in Britain, named for the pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Baltimore is a port city in Maryland, USA.

clue.text: Compiler's left standing by tribal forefather

indicators.note: standing in a down clue means read upwards

parts.note: the compiler (setter) says I have, written I've
L is left

explanation.surface: The setter has stood beside an ancestor of a tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' reverses IVEL; 'by' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Levi was a son of Jacob, the founder of one of Israel's twelve tribes.

clue.text: Language also adopted by serviceman, almost

indicators.note: adopted by means taken inside the following word
almost means the last letter is lost

parts.note: a marine is a serviceman
and means also

explanation.surface: A soldier picks up another tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts MARINE to MARIN, which takes in AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin is the main spoken Chinese tongue.

clue.text: Indian queen taken in by victim of strangulation?

indicators.note: taken in by means placed inside the following word

parts.note: a jocular coinage, one who is choked
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A queen is deceived by someone who was throttled.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the made-up word CHOKEE. 'taken in' looks like 'deceived' but is placement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cherokee are a Native American people, called Indians in older usage.

clue.text: Type of motion discovered by Bacon, Galileo, etc

indicators.note: discovered by means the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: A law of motion credited to the great early scientists.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests physics; the motion is a dance step, found across 'BaCON, GAlileo'.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin dance done in a snaking line, a kind of movement on the dance floor.

clue.text: Soldiers restored enclave's topicality

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of soldiers

indicators.note: restored means put back together in a new order

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: Troops rebuild a territory's importance in the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restored' signals the anagram; the RE (Royal Engineers) are a standard crossword source of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Relevance is the quality of bearing on current matters, a close synonym of topicality.

clue.text: Sister hops about on artificial leg, say

indicators.note: about means moved around, signalling an anagram of the words before it

explanation.surface: A nun skips around while wearing a false limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the ten letters of SISTER HOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosthesis is any artificial body part, and a false leg is one example, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Lose your figure, though having nothing for pudding

parts.note: to sag is to droop, as a body losing its shape
nothing is O, the zero

explanation.surface: A dieter gives up dessert for fear of losing their shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though having' joins the pieces; 'for' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch from palm pith, cooked with milk into a classic British milk pudding.

clue.text: Favourite turn by unknown in two sections

indicators.note: in means the unknown goes between the two section words

parts.note: a part is one section
a piece is another section
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A best-loved act performed by a stranger in two halves.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase, 'two sections', supplies both words that sandwich the unknown; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A party piece is a performer's favourite trick, the turn they always do when asked.

clue.text: Salute the Italian dead outside — or try to revive them with this?

definitions.text: try to revive them with this?

parts.note: a salvo is a firing of guns as a salute

indicators.note: outside means the word for dead goes around the next piece

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late king
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: Honour fallen Italians with gunfire, or bring them round with something under their noses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the Italian article in the dead word. The question mark warns that reviving the truly dead is a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Smelling salts were waved under a fainting person's nose to bring them round, so the dead might be tried with them.

clue.text: Victor's response to being tickled to death?

definitions.text: Victor's response to being tickled to death?

parts.words: Victor's response to being tickled to death?
parts.note: the winner's final triumph; and literally, the dying giggle of someone tickled until they expire

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the final triumph of whoever wins in the end, read here as a giggle at the moment of death.

clue.text: Force set off unpunished

indicators.note: off suggests something wrong or out of place, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A police unit lets someone go without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges FORCE SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting off scot-free means escaping any penalty.

clue.text: Manufacturer of piston in colour — red, initially

indicators.note: in means the piston goes inside the colour

parts.note: puce is a purplish brown colour
a piston rod drives an engine, so rod stands for piston

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of red

explanation.surface: A maker of pistons painted in red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' links; ROD goes 'in' PUCE, and 'initially' adds R.
explanation.definitionFit: A producer makes goods, just as a manufacturer does.

clue.text: Cautious PC cuts crime drastically

indicators.note: drastically suggests a violent reshaping, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A police officer slashes the local crime rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drastically' rearranges the eleven letters of PC CUTS CRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Being circumspect means looking around before acting, that is wary or careful.

clue.text: Second union flag hoisted by star

indicators.note: hoisted in a down clue means everything is read upwards

parts.note: S is second
U is union
a flag is an iris plant

explanation.surface: A second union flag is run up next to a star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoisted' turns SUIRIS upwards. The 'flag' is the yellow flag iris, not a banner; 'by' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius, the Dog Star, is the brightest star in the night sky.

clue.text: Confirm where to find cricket fan

parts.note: at gives the location where something is found
a keen cricket follower is found at a Test, the international match

explanation.surface: Ensure you know the place to spot a cricket enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match lasting up to five days.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness that something is true, to confirm it.

clue.text: Substantial orderly

definitions.meaning: large, as in a ... sum of money

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both considerable in amount and neat, as a tidy profit or a tidy room.

clue.text: Delicate situation where tree and river are set in stone

indicators.note: set in means placed inside, so the stone holds the tree and river

parts.note: flint is a hard stone
the ash is a tree
the Po is the river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A tense spot where a tree and a river are carved into rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set in' signals containment; 'where' is a link. The Po is a common crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashpoint is a place or moment where trouble is likely to erupt, a volatile state of affairs.

clue.text: Piece of Siberian timber, or piece of meat

indicators.note: piece of means take just a bit, here the first letter

parts.note: teak is a hardwood timber

explanation.surface: A chunk of Siberian wood or a slab of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A steak is a thick slice of beef or other meat.

clue.text: Examination about part of Israeli city

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: Aviv is part of Tel Aviv

explanation.surface: A test concerning a district of an Israeli city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns AVIV round.
explanation.definitionFit: A viva is an oral exam, short for viva voce, used for university degrees.

clue.text: City bird's inoffensive moral stance?

indicators.note: in means the city and the bird go inside the word for offensive

parts.note: rude means offensive
EC is the postcode of the City of London
a tit is a small bird

explanation.surface: A bird in the City is said to be harmless, a matter of good morals.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'inoffensive' as 'in offensive': the containment indicator is fused to the word it governs. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rectitude is uprightness of conduct, a principled ethical position.

clue.text: Drug with lo-calorie cream

parts.note: E is ecstasy, the drug
lite is the marketing spelling for low-calorie

explanation.surface: Medicine served with low-fat cream.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its best part, the select few at the top.

clue.text: Bank of Scotland returns remains of nag

indicators.note: returns means the bank's word is turned back

parts.note: a brae is a Scottish hillside or bank
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A Scottish bank gives back what is left of an old horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns BRAE into EARB. A brae is the Scots word for a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: To earbash is Australian slang for talking at someone relentlessly, so to nag.

clue.text: Knight catches monster dropping one in parliament

indicators.note: catches means holds within, so the knight goes around the monster
dropping means losing a letter

parts.note: Nessie is the Loch Ness monster
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A knight captures a monster that has lost one of its kind in a legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes I from NESSIE to give NESSE, which KT 'catches'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Knesset is Israel's national legislature, a specific parliament.
